Key observations from the test image:
- Split stems showing white/cream pith
- Heavy dark masses at the root/lower stem junction
- Roots appear dark and rotted
- No white fluffy mycelium visible

Top candidates: **Sudden_death_syndrome** (white pith + rotted roots), **Charcoal_Rot** (dark masses could be microsclerotia), **White_Mold** (black sclerotia)

The SDS reference shows a very similar bottom image - dark rotted root zone with split stems. White Mold can be ruled out (no fluffy white mycelium). Charcoal Rot shows reddish-brown pith, not white. Let me check Brown_Stem_Rot and Phytophthora to be thorough.

Now I have enough evidence to make my assessment.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Stems split lengthwise showing **white/cream pith**, heavy dark mass at the root/soil zone, severely rotted and decomposed root system.

- **Brown Stem Rot**: Reference shows **brown pith** when split — eliminated.

- **Charcoal Rot**: Would show reddish-brown pith and microsclerotia giving charcoal-sprinkled appearance internally — pith here is white, not brown — does not match well.

- **White Mold**: No fluffy white mycelium visible — eliminated.

- **Fusarium**: Reference shows similar dark root decay, but would have brown vascular tissue internally — test image pith is white.

- **Phytophthora**: Stem discoloration from soil line upward, different morphology — doesn't match.

- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Key diagnostic — **white pith** when cut (distinguishes from BSR), **rotted taproots and lateral roots**, heavy root decay. The SDS reference collage (bottom-left panel) shows a very similar plant with dark rotted root zone and split stems with white interior. This matches perfectly.
